TILCHE f *Environmental Engineering Department, Michigan State University, E. Lansing, MI 48824, U.S.A. tltalian Commission for Nuclear and Alternate Energy Sources, ENEA, CORELAB, DIM2, Via G. Mazzini 2, 40138 Bologna, Italy (Received 15 January 1992, accepted 3 March 1992) Abstract-An experimental study was undertaken to determine the effect of hydraulic retention time (HRT) on a 1501 hybrid anaerobic baffled reactor (HABR) at constant organic loading 10 kg m-' d-'. When the HRT was gradually changed from 1 day to 6 days, i.e. the feed concentration changed from 10 g 1-' to 60 g 1-', the COD reduction dropped from 75% to about 40%, the gas production rate decreased from 5.2 m' m-' d-' to 3.4 m' m-3 d-', and the efuent volatile fatty acids (VFA) concentration increased from 430 mg 1-' to about 16,000 mg 1-'. Thus methanogenic inhibition occurred at longer HRTs. The experimental results strongly suggested that the HRT is a significant factor for HABR performance. Keywords-Hydraulic retention time, anaerobic baffled reactor, anaerobic digestion, molasses waste treatment, constant organic loading, HABR, HRT. 1. INTRODUCTION Compared with organic loading, fermentation temperature, nutrient requirements and other potential physical and chemical fermentation inhibitors, hydraulic retention time, as a design and operation factor, is not as well elucidated in anaerobic digestion. However, recent publications have suggested that HRT could be important for upgrading anaerobic digester capability. Denac and Dunn' compared the anaerobic degradation performance of a lab-scale packed bed reactor (PBR) with two lab-scale fluidizedbed biofilm reactors (FBRs) treating molasses and whey feeds. In this study they found that at a constant loading 10 g 1-' d-' for both PBR and FBR, the COD reduction rates increased with HRT. For instance, when the HRT increased from 3 to 24 hr, the PBR COD reduction rate increased from 76% to about 90%, and the gas production rate increased from 5.51 d-' to 7.51 d-'. A similar result can be observed in research performed by Yan et al.,' in which a lab-scale UASB reactor was used for cheese whey wastes anaerobic digestion. The data presented in their report suggested that, for the same organic loading rate, the gas production was higher at longer HRT. For example, in their study when the HRT increased from 5 days to about 24 days at an organic loading 2 g 1-' d-', the gas production rate increased from 0.6781 g-' d-' to 1.0521 g-' d-'. In our recent research project, a 1501 working volume HABR was used for sugar plant molasses waste digestion. In this project, at a constant organic loading of 10 kg m-' d-', seven different HRTs were employed. The main purposes of this study are (1) to provide experimental evidence for the effect of HRT on HABR performance under constant organic loading, and (2) to obtain a better understanding of HABR hydraulic and kinetic characteristics. 2. MATERIALS AND METHODS 2.1. Apparatus The experiment Plexiglass HABR consisted of three chambers and a final settler (see Fig. 1). The working volume of each chamber was 501 and the total volume of this reactor including the settling tank was 1651. The first two chambers each had a 10 cm layer of plastic media (Pull rings D 38 mm, specific surface area 142 m2 m-3 and the void space 94%) near the liquid surface. In the third chamber the upper half was filled with a modular corrugated block (Eco Trick 200m' m-3, 98.5% void space). 25 26 Fig. 1. The waste was rich in protein but lacking in phosphorus. The molasses was concentrated in their factory for use as a fuel and therefore the COD concentration was very high. Analysis instruments and methods COD, pH, VFA, total alkalinity, gas production and composition were analyzed daily. The reactor profile was studied at the end of each test period by taking samples from each sampling point shown in Fig. 1. All the analyses were carried out according to standard methods.3 Gas production was measured for each chamber with three individual Elster Handel G.00 wet test gas meters. Experiment design At a constant organic loading 10 kg m-' d-', seven different HRT levels were employed in this study. The first test had a 1 day HRT, then it was gradually increased to 6 days. The organic loading was kept unchanged. At each HRT the experimental data were intensively collected during steady state condition. To minimize potential interferences, tap water was fed to the reactor for a while to drive out residue acids before each new test level began. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION The effects of increasing HRT on COD reduction and total gas and methane production are presented in Figs 2 and 3 respectively. Based on these results, at constant organic loading, the performance of the HABR was directly linked with operation HRT-in this case both COD reduction and total gas production decreased with the increasing HRT. Gas composition inside the reactor at longer HRTs. From this figure, it can be seen that at an HRT of 3.3 days, the first chamber effluent VFA concentration began to surpass the influent VFA concentration and at an HRT of 4.7 days the same phenomenon happened in the third chamber. The biogas composition as a function of HRT is shown in Fig. 5. Agreed with the VFA data, the gas composition changed significantly with HRT. For example, when the HRT increased from 1 day to 6 days, the content of CH, in the total biogas dropped from 73% to about 56%, while the content of COZ increased from 25.4% to 42%. In Fig. 6, a profile of VFA concentrations at five different HRT levels is given. The highest VFA concentrations occurred in the bottom of the first chamber where the feed molasses was injected into the HABR. In this experiment the actual organic loading of the first chamber was 30 kg m-3 d-'. Undoubtedly, under this condition, the dynamic balance between acid and methane producers was weak and sensitive. As Henze' pointed out, when an anaerobic digester is operated at its maximum load any sudden increase in easily degradable organics will result in an increased acid production and accumulation thereby inhibiting the methanogenesis. As shown in Fig. 5, with the first chamber VFA accumulation, a corresponding increase in the second and third chambers' effluent VFA concentrations occurred. The data available for HRT-efficiency analysis were obtained at a constant organic loading 10 g 1-' d-'. The other research project quoted in this paper was undertaken by Yan et al.,' where a 17.51 working volume lab-scale UASB reactor was used to treat cheese whey waste. The experimental data presented in their report were obtained from an organic loading range of 1 to 4 g 1-' d-'. Obviously, in these experiments the digesters were operated at relatively low organic loadings; in this condition increasing HRT tends to increase the reaction driving force,' thus increasing the COD reduction and biogas production rates. 4. CONCLUSIONS 4. 5. The experimental results presented here fi suggest that hydraulic retention time is signifi- cant for optimizing performance of HABR as 29 well as other anaerobic digesters. The effect is positive or negative depending on the organic loading rate.
